results.previous_best: DGG99: $y_a < x_a + d_{\max}$ for single-source unsplittable flows (SSUF)
results.quote: Given a b-transshipment x, the Modified DGG Algorithm efficiently computes an unsplittable transshipment such that the flow on each arc a is strictly less than x_a+d_max.
Under the balance condition, the Modified DGG Algorithm yields a 2-approximation algorithm for minimizing congestion in unsplittable transshipment instances.

results.bound: arc capacity violation $\le \min\{\max_{s\in S^+} b(s), \max_{t\in S^-} |b(t)|\}$
results.quote: Reversing all arcs yields a maximum capacity violation of at most max_{s\in S^+}b(s). Thus, the Modified DGG Algorithm computes, in polynomial time, an unsplittable transshipment whose arc capacity violation is bounded by the minimum of the maximum supply max_{s\in S^+}b(s) and the maximum demand max_{t\in S^-}|b(t)|.

results.problem: Unsplittable Transshipment Problem (lower bounds on arc flows)
results.quote: Given a b-transshipment x, the adapted Modified DGG Algorithm efficiently computes an unsplittable transshipment such that the flow on each arc a is greater than x_a-d_max.

results.bound: at most $|S^+| + |S^-| - 1$ paths (edges in the source-sink bipartite graph)
results.previous_best: an arbitrary unsplittable transshipment may use up to $|S^+|\cdot|S^-|$ paths
results.quote: the bipartite graph associated with any unsplittable transshipment computed by the Modified DGG Algorithm is acyclic, and thus contains at most |S^+|+|S^-|-1 edges.

results.bound: $d_{\max}$ capacity violation is unavoidable (tight) even when every sink is connected to arbitrarily many sources
results.previous_best: DGG99 showed tightness of $d_{\max}$ for SSUF
results.quote: Thus, even when each sink is connected to arbitrarily many sources, no unsplittable transshipment can avoid a violation of d_max, establishing the tightness of the bound.

results.problem: Cost of Confluence in unsplittable transshipment
results.bound: any confluent unsplittable transshipment has congestion at least $1 - 1/q$, tending to $d_{\max} = 1$ as $q \to \infty$
results.quote: Hence, in any confluent unsplittable transshipment, the capacity violation on that arc is at least 1-1/q, which tends to d_max=1 as q\rightarrow\infty.

results.problem: Minimum number of rounds for unsplittable transshipment
results.previous_best: DGG99: 5 rounds for SSUF; no general constant bounds for transshipment
results.quote: the total number of routing rounds is (n+1)\cdot(N_tot+1).

results.problem: Minimum number of rounds for unsplittable transshipment
results.quote: Therefore, if d_max\le c_min/3, then all demands can be routed unsplittably in six rounds.

results.problem: Minimum number of rounds for unsplittable transshipment
results.quote: Critically split sinks with the same label are grouped, and their paths are superimposed to form two additional rounds. No finer grouping is required for feasibility as c_a/2+d_max+d_max\le c_a/2+c_min/2\le c_a.

results.problem: Maximum routable demand for unsplittable transshipment
results.bound: at least $0.07143 \cdot d_{\text{tot}}$ total demand can be routed (under $d_{\max} \le \tfrac12 b_{\text{avg}}^+$)
results.quote: the maximum routable demand is lower bounded by max{d/6,1-d/8}\cdot d_tot for d\in[0,1], which attains its minimum at d=3/7 and is therefore always at least 0.07143\cdot d_tot.
